Which temple should I visit on Koh Samui? | If you see only one, make it Big Buddha with Wat Plai Laem 1 km away; with a second half day, add the south: the Red Temple, the Guan Yu Shrine, Wat Khunaram and Laem Sor Pagoda.
Is the Big Buddha free to visit? | Yes, Big Buddha is free and open 07:00–18:30; all the main temples on Koh Samui are free, and only the private Secret Buddha Garden charges 80–100 THB.
What should I wear to temples on Koh Samui? | Cover shoulders and knees, avoid beachwear, and carry a sarong; take your shoes off before entering halls and on some platforms.
Can I see the mummified monk? | Yes, at Wat Khunaram on the ring road in Na Mueang; entry is free, he sits in a glass case in his own hall, and respectful photos without flash are generally allowed.
Where is the Red Temple? | On the ring road about 2 km south of central Lamai, between Hin Ta and Hin Yai and Hua Thanon; its official name is Wat Ratchathammaram.
Are Koh Samui temples open every day? | Yes, the main temples open daily, roughly 07:00 to 17:00–18:30, but halls can close for ceremonies and hours shift on Buddhist holidays.
Can I take photos inside temples on Koh Samui? | Outdoors yes; inside, follow the signs, turn off flash, never pose disrespectfully with Buddha images and ask before photographing monks or worshippers.
Can women visit temples and speak to monks? | Yes, women can visit every temple and talk to monks, but should not touch a monk or hand him anything directly; place it on a cloth or table instead.
When is Loy Krathong on Koh Samui? | Tuesday 24 November 2026; the main spots are Chaweng Lake and Big Buddha, sky lanterns are banned on Samui, and the 2027 date is expected to be Saturday 13 November.
Can I join a meditation session at a temple? | Most Samui temples don't run drop-in classes, but you can sit quietly in any hall; for guided practice, book a meditation centre or retreat with a fixed schedule.
Is there a dress code at Chinese shrines on Koh Samui? | Yes, the same respectful dress applies: shoulders and knees covered; offer incense with both hands and never blow it out.
Which Buddhist holidays ban alcohol sales on Koh Samui in 2027? | Makha Bucha (21 Feb), Visakha Bucha (20 May), Asahna Bucha and Khao Phansa (about 18–19 Jul) and Ok Phansa (about 15 Oct); hotels and licensed bars may still serve.
